extractedText: Productivity11 Best AI Workflow Automation Tools for 2026Explore 11 of the top AI workflow automation tools and learn how to choose the best one for your business.By the team at SlackDecember 10th, 2025Table of ContentsTable of Contents 10 min readKey takeawaysAI workflow automation tools offer unique features that are ideal for different teams and use cases. The right AI workflow automation tool for your business will address a specific need and be easy to incorporate into your existing workflows. AI workflow automation tools meet multiple business needs, from task management to agentic support and more. Between meetings, deadlines, reports, and your actual work, it can seem like there’s never enough time in a workday. The transformative power of automation and AI productivity tools can help. These innovative tools can rapidly perform tasks that otherwise take several minutes or even hours, freeing you up for more creative, high-value work. We’ve put together a list of top AI workflow automation tools — each with its own key features, capabilities, and benefits — to help you find the one that fits your team’s goals. The list is curated from reviews on G2 and Capterra, and all tools have a minimum rating of 4 out of 5 stars to ensure you’re getting a high-quality solution. 1. Agentforce in Slack Slack organizes and unifies data in a single work operating system, connecting teams with the people and tools they use every day. Agentforce is Salesforce’s agentic AI platform, designed to empower organizations to build, customize, and deploy AI agents. When deployed in Slack, users can engage with employee-facing agents directly in their flow of work. For example, teams can communicate with agents and assign them tasks directly in Slack, just as they would a human co-worker, making the agents collaborative virtual teammates that help increase productivity. Best for: Teams looking to enhance how they work and collaborate in a centralized work OS. 2. Trello Trello is a project management software tool that allows users to create a visual set of lists, or boards, to organize project tasks. Trello features AI tools, including an analyst agent that examines existing Trello boards for trends and insights that can help teams with workflow management. With the report generator, users can type in a prompt and get a report based on the board they’re viewing. This helps teams get the information they need for efficient decision-making. The premium version also offers an AI writing assistant and other organizational tools. Best for: Teams aiming to combine the visual aid of a Kanban board with AI-supported efficiencies. 3. Zapier Zapier is a popular workflow automation tool that connects with more than 7,000 apps. Users say it’s easy to use and that they can automate workflows involving multiple software tools — including Salesforce, Slack, Mailchimp, HubSpot, and many more — in one place. Zapier includes integrated AI tools to help users build new workflows, identify trends in data, and summarize meeting transcripts. It also connects to external AI apps, such as Jasper and ChatGPT, allowing teams to automate content creation like email campaigns and blog post drafts. Best for: Lean organizations that need a quick, intuitive way to build workflows across multiple apps. 4. Asana Asana is a project management platform that helps teams plan and organize complex projects and tasks, from marketing campaigns to product development. Asana has integrated AI tools, including one where users can use a no-code builder to design AI agents. This lets users share work with purpose-built agents. With Asana, you can also automate multiple workflow stages, from intake to reporting to drafting content, keeping projects moving forward. Best for: Organizations seeking a flexible, broadly applicable project management tool capable of integrating AI workflows for all users. 5. HubSpot HubSpot is a full CRM platform, serving sales, marketing, content management, customer service, and more. It includes several AI features to help users automate marketing tasks, such as creating social media posts, drafting prospect emails, and implementing customer agent chatbots. Users can also use AI tools to analyze sales and customer data, discern buyer intent, and build optimized forms. Best for: Organizations looking to elevate their customer-facing teams with intelligent workflows. 6. Google Cloud AI Google Cloud’s AI Hub gives users access to plug-and-play AI tools that they can use to build AI models, integrate with other software, and share what they’ve created. With generative AI capabilities, teams can create a range of agents and applications that are trained on their organization’s data. They can then interact with those agents to accomplish various tasks such as extracting insights from lengthy documents, building custom machine learning models, and conducting data analysis.
